_doc: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the selection-time task-rejection gate.
Read by select/task_gates.py (selection + materialization) and by
harness/task-gates.mjs (run-pilot's defense-in-depth preflight WARN).
Change the numbers HERE and nowhere else.
The gate is METADATA-ONLY and OUTCOME-BLIND: it looks at FAIL_TO_PASS /
PASS_TO_PASS list lengths in the task spec, never at a run result, never at
sweet-vs-native. That is what keeps it pre-registration compatible.
WHY these two rules (PLAN.md §1.3 — 'tasks whose whole suite is red at
baseline'). On such tasks 'solving' means repairing the build, not fixing the
bug, so the benchmark measures build-wrangling instead of the thing we claim
to measure:
max_fail_to_pass = 100
spectreconsole__spectre.console-1942  F2P=495  (native 'won' it by
rewriting net9.0 across every .csproj)
hyperledger__firefly-716              F2P=293
mwouts__jupytext-360                  F2P=33   (under the threshold; it is
caught by nothing here and stays a judgement call — the threshold is set
where whole-suite failure is unambiguous, not where it first smells)
min_pass_to_pass = 1  (i.e. reject PASS_TO_PASS == 0)
btcpayserver__btcpayserver-6251       F2P=21 with P2P=0 — compile-gated:
the hidden TestAccount.cs helper calls the new GeneralSettings(storeId)
signature, so ANY patch that does not change that signature fails the
whole assembly 21/21.
CAVEAT ON min_pass_to_pass, recorded so the next reader does not have to
rediscover it: P2P==0 is a stricter rule than the btcpay case alone requires.
On the three current populations it rejects ~20% of candidates, and for some
of those (e.g. F2P=1, P2P=0) the empty PASS_TO_PASS looks like a dataset
recording artifact rather than a red suite. It is kept because a task with no
verified-passing baseline test gives the grader no regression signal at all,
and because rejection is CHEAP: the gate runs against a ~19k-task pool, so a
rejected candidate is simply replaced by the next draw of the same seeded
shuffle. It costs pool size, never set size.
reject_name_locked = true  (added 2026-08-24)
A task is NAME-LOCKED when its hidden test imports an identifier that the
reference patch INVENTED, that the base tree never mentions, and that the issue
text does not spell out. An agent that produces a functionally identical fix
under any other name FAILS, so the task measures a naming lottery and no
analyzer, index, ranking change or certificate can close the gap.
joshuakgoldberg__bingo-274  hidden test: import { isFile } from './isFile.js'
dart-lang__http-1114        hidden test: response.headersSplitValues
Both flip at NO hint level, a full prose specification of the required
behaviour included, and a 20x-larger backbone buys 0/10 on one of them
(HINT-LADDER-RESULTS.md). 4 of the 18 current rotation tasks are locked.
UNLIKE the two rules above, this one cannot be computed from the task record
alone: deciding 'invented' needs the BASE TREE. So it is computed once at
RECRUITMENT by select/stamp-name-lock.mjs, which needs gold and a materialized
checkout, and STAMPED into the record as `name_locked`. Everything downstream
reads the stamped boolean, which keeps this gate metadata-only and outcome-blind
exactly like the other two. An UNSTAMPED task is never rejected: absence of the
field means not-yet-measured, never clean.
